title: BEQDesigner review queue entry
description: One file in a pipeline.review queue directory (design/candidate-review-plan.md), named '<id>.json'. Written by pipeline.review.batch_design()/write_queue_entry() and read/updated by the same module and by model/review.py's ReviewQueueDialog (Tools > Review Batch Designs). Plain (non-gzipped) UTF-8 JSON.

id.description: stable slug for this title, also the filename (id + '.json')

fs.description: publish-target sample rate (Hz) the candidates' filters were realised at

meta.description: pipeline.metadata.BeqMetadata *constructor* kwargs (title/year/audio_types/genres/...), not its beq_-prefixed to_json()/to_dict() XML-ready shape -- BeqMetadata(**meta) must reconstruct it. May be partial/empty if title metadata (e.g. a TMDB lookup) hasn't been resolved yet.

curve.description: one unfiltered magnitude curve (avg), via model.codec.xydata_to_json -- enough to redraw a live preview without the original audio.

candidates.description: empty when declined (see decline_reason/decline_message). Otherwise non-empty, ordered best (most preferred) first -- candidates[0] is the designer's top pick.

decline_reason.description: set together with decline_message, candidates left empty, when the designer declined this title -- design/designer-interface.md §4

status.description: pending: awaiting review. accepted: a human picked candidates[chosen_candidate_index]. skipped: deferred, still pending in spirit -- come back to it later. rejected: a human's permanent no, distinct from skipped. published: an accepted entry that publish_reviewed_queue() has already pushed -- re-running is then a no-op for this entry.

chosen_candidate_index.description: required, and must index into candidates, when status is 'accepted' or 'published'; null/absent otherwise

reviewer_note.description: free text a human reviewer left on this entry; not used by any pipeline code

art_path.description: local image file path used as this entry's report poster, if any -- set by a human via the review dialog's Artwork section, or auto-resolved by a library run (the library source's own image, else TMDB's poster downloaded into the item's work directory). null if none.

art_overridden.description: true once a human has explicitly set art_path -- auto-resolution must never silently overwrite it. The review dialog's Clear resets this to false, returning the entry to automatic resolution the next time it is redesigned.

design_fingerprint.description: opaque hash of the source fingerprint, designer, analysis configuration, and coverage that produced this entry. Absent on queues written before library caching; those entries are deliberately treated as stale once.

published_digest.description: opaque hash of everything the catalogue entry was built from when this entry became 'published': the published filter (a hand-edited .beq project's, else the chosen candidate's), the metadata, the artwork file's content, whether an image was made, and the master-volume offset. A different hash computed now means what was published is out of date. Absent on entries published before this field existed.

published_at.description: UTC ISO-8601 time the entry became 'published'. 'published' means the XML (and image) were written into the catalogue repos' working trees; whether they are committed or pushed is read from git and is not stored here (the one-step publish, pipeline.review.publish_reviewed_queue() with push=True, does commit and push each file as it writes it).

candidateSummary.description: One candidate's filters (already realised at the entry's fs) plus the provenance a reviewer needs to judge it -- pipeline.review.CandidateSummary.

filters.description: the candidate's filters, already realised at fs -- the same shape as a published .filter file (filter.schema.json).

confidence.description: ordinal in v1 (design/designer-interface.md §3) -- comparable within this entry's candidates list, not across titles

mv_adjust_db.description: the cascade's implied gain (catalogue mv_adjust compatibility) -- NOT a clipping-cost estimate, see gain_reduction_db

gain_reduction_db.description: the actual clipping-cost figure: min(20*log10(1/peak), 0) of the filtered sub feed. Always <= 0; null if not computed.

commentary.description: structured, human-facing notes about this candidate -- dict[str, str], rendered as-is; not machine-parsed.
